 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0030e9c2-097f-42d5-8281-67219c0ea4fe",
   "metadata": {

     "slide_type": ""

    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "# 20260917 - Perf and Topdown Microarchitecture Analysis (Lab 3)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e008dc9f-8278-48cf-94e9-d6d3c9771555",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "## Bruteforce\n",
    "\n",
    "From [lab 3](https://github.com/CU-HPSC-Fall-2026/cu-hpsc-lab3), we had the following bruteforce computation for the madelbrot set:\n",
    "\n",
    "```c\n",
    "  // iterate over map\n",
    "  for (long indf = 0; indf < args.max_iter; ++indf) {\n",
    "    // apply function to each grid point\n",
    "    for (long indA = 0; indA < numA; ++indA) {\n",
    "      for (long indB = 0; indB < numB; ++indB) {\n",
    "        long indAB = indA * numB + indB;\n",
    "        double scratch = MMAP_REAL(A[indAB], B[indAB], A_0[indA]);\n",
    "        B[indAB] = MMAP_IMAG(A[indAB], B[indAB], B_0[indB]);\n",
    "        A[indAB] = scratch;\n",
    "      }\n",
    "    }\n",
    "  }\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "- We loop over function iterations, then over points."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 17,
   "id": "873b6407-36c4-4477-afd1-550bbea96095",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "bruteforce_noswap = pd.read_csv(\"./bruteforce_serial_noswap.csv\")\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots()\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_noswap['d'], bruteforce_noswap['map/s'])\n",
    "ax.set_xscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_yscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('density, d')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('map/s')\n",
    "ax.grid();"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "af5bf9c2-820e-43b7-aa33-4b2d66b57a7e",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Theoretically, our arithmetic intensity should be incredibly high.\n",
    "- We do 1000 iterations for each point, each iteration is 7 FLOPs\n",
    "- This should be a theoretical FLOP/byte of\n",
    "$$ \\frac{7000 FLOP}{16 byte} \\approx 437$$\n",
    "- But we're still clearly in memory-bound computation\n",
    "\n",
    "Why?"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "110e2868-f31a-4759-a7f8-14cb41e6c3e5",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "**Loop ordering**\n",
    "\n",
    "- Arithmetic intensity is not about the total bytes and total FLOPs\n",
    "- **It is the FLOPs you execute while the data is in registers/L1 cache**\n",
    "\n",
    "- By looping over iterations first, we're actually moving the point data `m` times.\n",
    "    - Thus, our actual arithmetic intensity is\n",
    "$$\\frac{7 FLOP}{16 byte} \\approx 0.4375$$"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "769a1a2e-d0d8-4441-b565-00cdfeb729d8",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "If we change the loop order to have iterations inside:\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "```c\n",
    "  // iterate over map\n",
    "  for (long indA = 0; indA < numA; ++indA) {\n",
    "    for (long indB = 0; indB < numB; ++indB) {\n",
    "      // apply function to each grid point\n",
    "      for (long indf = 0; indf < args.max_iter; ++indf) {\n",
    "        long indAB = indA * numB + indB;\n",
    "        double scratch = MMAP_REAL(A[indAB], B[indAB], A_0[indA]);\n",
    "        B[indAB] = MMAP_IMAG(A[indAB], B[indAB], B_0[indB]);\n",
    "        A[indAB] = scratch;\n",
    "      }\n",
    "    }\n",
    "  }\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "Now we get"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 18,
   "id": "639f39e8-e038-4c30-87db-6ef8a46ce4e5",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "bruteforce_swap = pd.read_csv(\"./bruteforce_serial_swap.csv\")\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots()\n",
    "\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_noswap['d'], bruteforce_noswap['map/s'], label='original')\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_swap['d'], bruteforce_swap['map/s'], label='swapped loop order')\n",
    "ax.set_xscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_yscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('density, d')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('map/s')\n",
    "ax.grid()\n",
    "ax.legend();"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "8f05ed44-0b65-47b3-9bf7-6a27a29110c3",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "- The performance is (nearly) constant (excluding the smallest density\n",
    "    - Thus, we are in the compute-bound regime now!\n",
    "    - Our actual arithmetic intensity is the \"real\" 423 FLOPs/byte"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "66905ab9-3a1d-4577-b5d7-c421e81719a5",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "**Why is the original faster at smaller densities though?**"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0c49eaf2-712c-4ea7-a5fe-f1b0c6a24c9b",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": ""
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "## How would we figure this out?\n",
    "\n",
    "We can use `perf` to figure out what is happening, focusing on Top-down Microarchitecture Analysis (TMA)\n",
    "- TMA is a way of categorizing what is preventing the CPU from going faster\n",
    "- It puts the time the CPU is spending into a hierarchy of categories\n",
    "- Originally introduced in [*A Top-Down method for performance analysis and counters architecture*](https://doi-org.colorado.idm.oclc.org/10.1109/ISPASS.2014.6844459)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b2fcc68d-f85d-4c74-ad59-f54a23ed09eb",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Here is the top-most level hierarchy:\n",
    "\n",
    "| Level | Meaning |\n",
    "| --- | --- |\n",
    "| Retiring | This represents cycles spent on instructions that were successfully completed. This is the ideal case. |\n",
    "| Frontend Bound | This represents stalls occurring because the CPU cannot fetch or decode instructions fast enough to keep the backend busy. |\n",
    "| Backend Bound | This represents stalls occurring because the execution units are busy or waiting for data (e.g., memory latency or bandwidth issues). |\n",
    "| Bad Speculation | This represents work wasted on instructions that were executed but eventually discarded due to branch mispredictions or other pipeline flushes. |"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4fa676db-9783-426e-b554-4a6185e7275a",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "![TMA Diagram](https://yukunj.github.io/images/blogs/tma.png)\n",
    "\n",
    "Blog: https://yukunj.github.io/blogs/tma"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "01c366dd-2d0b-4fce-a0b3-d831a89edc56",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### Using `perf` for TMA\n",
    "\n",
    "Start by running the program with\n",
    "```\n",
    "perf stat <program>\n",
    "```\n",
    "For example:\n",
    "```\n",
    "$ perf stat ./mandelbrot_bruteforce_blocked -d 100 > /dev/null\n",
    "[...]\n",
    "Performance counter stats for './mandelbrot_bruteforce_blocked -d 100':\n",
    "\n",
    "                 1      context-switches                 #      4.9 cs/sec  cs_per_second\n",
    "                 0      cpu-migrations                   #      0.0 migrations/sec  migrations_per_second\n",
    "               382      page-faults                      #   1855.4 faults/sec  page_faults_per_second\n",
    "            205.89 msec task-clock                       #      nan CPUs  CPUs_utilized\n",
    "            14,592      branch-misses                    #      0.0 %  branch_miss_rate\n",
    "       104,569,656      branches                         #    507.9 M/sec  branch_frequency\n",
    "       840,910,525      cpu-cycles                       #      4.1 GHz  cycles_frequency\n",
    "     1,639,739,158      instructions                     #      1.9 instructions  insn_per_cycle\n",
    "            TopdownL1 #     47.5 %  tma_backend_bound\n",
    "                                                         #      0.8 %  tma_bad_speculation\n",
    "                                                         #      8.6 %  tma_frontend_bound\n",
    "                                                         #     43.1 %  tma_retiring\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "The `# <number> % tma_*` gives information about the time spent by the CPU in each category."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2bee7f06-af6f-4a7e-9587-0f8a5025d75c",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "To drill further, we can run \n",
    "\n",
    "```\n",
    "perf stat -M tma_*_group <program>\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "where the `*` gets replaced by whatever specific group you want to know information about.\n",
    "This allows us to do deeper into the hierarchy.\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "<div class=\"alert alert-block alert-info\">\n",
    "<b></b> \n",
    "If you want more information about a specific group or what it means, search for it in `perf list -v`.\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a33171b0-a6e1-412d-a539-5897d9d81c20",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Drilling down, we end up looking at port utilization\n",
    "- `tma_ports_utilized_*` indicates the percent of the time where the CPU cores were doing 0, 1, 2 or 3 $\\mu$ops\n",
    "    - The more $\\mu$ops we do at once, the faster we perform our computations\n",
    "\n",
    "**Normal Bruteforce:**\n",
    "```\n",
    "$ sudo perf stat -M tma_ports_utilization_group ./mandelbrot_bruteforce -d 100 > /dev/null\n",
    "[....]\n",
    "       665,182,876      TOPDOWN.SLOTS                    #      0.2 %  tma_ports_utilized_0\n",
    "                                                         #     12.5 %  tma_ports_utilized_1\n",
    "                                                         #     18.6 %  tma_ports_utilized_2     (88.73%)\n",
    "        81,736,062      UOPS_EXECUTED.CYCLES_GE_3        #     60.4 %  tma_ports_utilized_3m    (88.72%)\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "**Swapped Bruteforce:**\n",
    "```\n",
    "$ sudo perf stat -M tma_ports_utilization_group ./mandelbrot_bruteforce_swap -d 100 > /dev/null\n",
    "[....]\n",
    "     1,173,759,662      TOPDOWN.SLOTS                    #     34.3 %  tma_ports_utilized_0\n",
    "                                                         #     43.3 %  tma_ports_utilized_1\n",
    "                                                         #      8.9 %  tma_ports_utilized_2     (89.97%)\n",
    "        25,922,080      UOPS_EXECUTED.CYCLES_GE_3        #     11.0 %  tma_ports_utilized_3m    (89.99%)\n",
    "```\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "26f4b847-914f-4c46-8fdb-a27be4de2b9f",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Normal bruteforce gets better ILP!\n",
    "\n",
    "- By having the outer loop over iterations, each inner loop is completely independent!\n",
    "    - Thus, the CPU can dispatch every instruction in that loop independently of the next\n",
    "    \n",
    "```c\n",
    "  for (long indf = 0; indf < args.max_iter; ++indf) {\n",
    "    for (long indA = 0; indA < numA; ++indA) {\n",
    "      for (long indB = 0; indB < numB; ++indB) {\n",
    "        long indAB = indA * numB + indB;\n",
    "        double scratch = MMAP_REAL(A[indAB], B[indAB], A_0[indA]);\n",
    "        B[indAB] = MMAP_IMAG(A[indAB], B[indAB], B_0[indB]);\n",
    "        A[indAB] = scratch;\n",
    "      }\n",
    "    }\n",
    "  }\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "43e6398b-8fb9-48cc-b3b9-323a401972cb",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "## Blocked\n",
    "\n",
    "What if we combined the two stratgies?\n",
    "- Ensure the inner-most loop has independent data\n",
    "- Ensure that computations are done while required data are located in cache"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2389a372-c771-4784-96dc-549e28e8eaba",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "This is sometimes known as **blocking**.\n",
    "- We divide the data to be computed on into blocks\n",
    "- Then we operate on those blocks while the data is in cache"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e8b05771-e75a-4065-8c5d-eec27190bf88",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    " The easiest way for us to do that is simply put the iteration loop between our row loop and our column loop:\n",
    "```c\n",
    "  for (long indA = 0; indA < numA; ++indA) {\n",
    "    for (long indf = 0; indf < args.max_iter; ++indf) {\n",
    "      for (long indB = 0; indB < numB; ++indB) {\n",
    "        long indAB = indA * numB + indB;\n",
    "        double scratch = MMAP_REAL(A[indAB], B[indAB], A_0[indA]);\n",
    "        B[indAB] = MMAP_IMAG(A[indAB], B[indAB], B_0[indB]);\n",
    "        A[indAB] = scratch;\n",
    "      }\n",
    "    }\n",
    "  }\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 19,
   "id": "add3618b-e59c-4911-88e3-060528fd6fce",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": ""
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "bruteforce_blocked = pd.read_csv(\"./bruteforce_serial_blocked.csv\")\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots()\n",
    "\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_noswap['d'], bruteforce_noswap['map/s'], label='original')\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_swap['d'], bruteforce_swap['map/s'], label='swapped loop order')\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_blocked['d'], bruteforce_blocked['map/s'], label='blocked')\n",
    "ax.set_xscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_yscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('density, d')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('map/s')\n",
    "ax.grid()\n",
    "ax.legend();"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0baf66ab-7602-476e-abbb-c9da4843236f",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": ""
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "We get the best of both worlds!\n",
    "- We get the best performance at small densities\n",
    "- We get the best performance at large densities\n",
    "- The performance is completely independent of the computation being done!"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b97c3113-1af3-44ae-9fab-7feb6330e832",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### Different form of blocked\n",
    "\n",
    "What if we wanted to block by some arbitrary amount rather than by rows?\n",
    "- For instance, maybe the size of each row exceeds L1 cache\n",
    "\n",
    "Could we instead\n",
    "\n",
    "```c\n",
    "#define BLOCK_SIZE 80000\n",
    "  // iterate over map\n",
    "  for (long block = 0; block < numA * numB / BLOCK_SIZE; ++block) {\n",
    "    long indAB_start = block * BLOCK_SIZE;\n",
    "    long indAB_stop = (block + 1) * BLOCK_SIZE;\n",
    "    if (indAB_stop > numA * numB)\n",
    "      indAB_stop = numA * numB;\n",
    "    for (long indf = 0; indf < max_iter; ++indf) {\n",
    "      for (long indAB = indAB_start; indAB < indAB_stop; ++indAB) {\n",
    "\n",
    "        long indA = indAB / numB;\n",
    "        long indB = indAB % numB;\n",
    "        double scratch = MMAP_REAL(A[indAB], B[indAB], A_0[indA]);\n",
    "        B[indAB] = MMAP_IMAG(A[indAB], B[indAB], B_0[indB]);\n",
    "        A[indAB] = scratch;\n",
    "      }\n",
    "    }\n",
    "  }\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 21,
   "id": "7eddd066-8455-48ba-a21c-d33c3f7065d4",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "bruteforce_blocked_flex = pd.read_csv(\"./bruteforce_serial_blocked_flex.csv\")\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots()\n",
    "\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_noswap['d'], bruteforce_noswap['map/s'], label='original')\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_swap['d'], bruteforce_swap['map/s'], label='swapped loop order')\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_blocked['d'], bruteforce_blocked['map/s'], label='blocked')\n",
    "ax.plot(bruteforce_blocked_flex['d'][2:], bruteforce_blocked_flex['map/s'][2:], label='blocked flexible')\n",
    "ax.set_xscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_yscale('log')\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('density, d')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel('map/s')\n",
    "ax.grid()\n",
    "ax.legend();"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "1eb8fc5a-1781-491e-9e48-1ff5bd29511f",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Why are we getting so much lower?\n",
    "\n",
    "Back to perf!"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "425a5361-1a94-4591-9349-5a181264b51b",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### `perf record`\n",
    "\n",
    "This allows us to get a much closer examination into exactly where in the code time is being taken.\n",
    "Two set process:\n",
    "1. Record the execution of the event\n",
    "2. Examine the resulting data"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d304b2f8-73da-4c7e-889d-a7ffd2d45038",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "To record simply\n",
    "\n",
    "```\n",
    "perf record <program>\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "This outputs a `perf.data` file"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a03601b6-f717-4982-bdf0-d13f345da0cd",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "raw_mimetype": "",
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Then, to examine, we use `perf report`.\n",
    "- This automatically looks for a `perf.data` file and reads that out\n",
    "\n",
    "**Annotate Assembly**\n",
    "- Perf can tell use exactly which instructions spent the most time executing\n",
    "    - Use `<Tab>` and `<Shift> + <Tab>` to go between the longest running instructions\n",
    "- Jump instructions also annotated\n",
    "\n",
    "**Vector Instructions vs Scalar Instructions**\n",
    "- `*sd` instructions means \"scalar double\" instructions, indicating lack of vectorization.\n",
    "- `*pd` \"packed double\" instructions, which are vectorized instructions"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7de12fd9-4fd3-446c-b01b-ec02968c089d",
   "metadata": {
    "editable": true,
    "jp-MarkdownHeadingCollapsed": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### Vectorization fails\n",
    "\n",
    "- We see that the flexible version of blocked fails to vectorize the inner loop\n",
    "    - Most time spent in `*sd` instructions\n",
    "    - While the row-based blocking spends it's time in the `*pd` instructions\n",
    "- Even with `#pragma omp simd`, still don't get vectorization\n",
    "- Some possible reasons (in order from most likely to least likely, in my opinion)\n",
    "    - Can't follow the memory access pattern (with the integer division and modulo operator)\n",
    "        - Previously the `long indAB = indA * numB + indB;` indexing was done\n",
    "        - This is a *very* common pattern (even if not done explicitly by the programmer), so the compiler can pick up on what the intention is\n",
    "        - By comparison, doing the integer division/modulo is not very common and is a bit more obtuse\n",
    "    - Integer division/modulo is slow, which means the compiler doesn't see value in vectorization\n",
    "    - Attempts and fails to vectorize the integer division and modulo operators"
   ]
  }
